I was not able to think of anything, love overcame everything. Oh, my Love! He made me feel, he was in me and said:

  • I live in you!

As I recovered, I said:

  • My Good, for pity’s sake, hold tightly this son of yours;

take care of him and do not let him shift from your side, where one day I may see him in your arms, safe for an eternity!

90 Oh, suffering, which united with the love of my Good, is felt in me in such a way that I cannot describe! || Alone, in this earth of exile, shaken by every kind of pain, you my Beloved Good, turn to sweetness the cruel torments that I receive from every side.

I embraced my Crucifix and continued to show him my deep wounds. Oh, what comfort he gave me! I must say that from when my son left, his sensible support has been continuous: now he assures me of his salvation, now he shows me his return and now his death as a true Christian.

And what my heart felt was to exult with joy! Oh, how much affection is experienced in you, Life of my life, Being of my life! You alone, alone, you are enough for me for the whole world!

A night together with Mary, the dear Mother

Date 24 (…) 1876.What I suffered last night! Oh, only you my Love could make me write! I was tormented cruelly by the ugly beasts in different shapes: big, horrendous and close to me. || They went around me as if they wanted to 91 catch me, what pain is this! To see that they came close and to be unable to say anything, what a torture! I felt as if my throat was tight as if someone was binding me and after forcing myself or rather, when it pleased my Good that I would be unbound, then I gained strength and I asked who they were, what they wanted, and I ordered them to go away. But before this, what a pain my God, it is cruel. I cannot move, not even to sign myself, as if an invisible power kept me tied, and sometimes I stay for long. I can only wake up, and this I do often; I sit down on the bed but am very frightened.

It is funny when I start to ask them something and to command them. || Oh, how funny! 92 In running away they fall one upon another, and they stimulate me to laughter.

What cruel sorrows I had to go through today! I do not say by whom and why: it is very unusual. And the person? Enough! May God give me the strength to bear such suffering and fill with every good whoever uses such “charity” towards me!

I felt a terrible anxiety, but God did not delay to come and comfort me: Oh, my Love, my side, my bones! As I said this, I was enraptured.

(I resume)

I spent the night together with my dear Mother Mary. She clasped me close all night long; she comforted me, and I felt something peaceful descend on me, resignation and strength to be able to continue my work the next day. 93 First, she exhorted me and gave me lovely lessons, then she assured me || that what I was suffering was very dear to Jesus and that he was with me. Oh, sweetest mother! Now she showed me Jesus always in an act of comforting me and pitying me. At the end, her words fell down straight into my soul, and often when I come back to myself, I could not do other than exclaim: Alas, I am dying.

My side was in such a way, that I cannot express, what a torture of love! The next day full of energy, nothing could knock me down; even the cruelest torments I lived in my Love. Oh, dear Mary, my dearest Mother! I found everything easy, because I had great lights and knowledge and I acted with vigour and without fear; and when another cross approached me I repeated: New day, new cross. 94 All the pains seemed to me nothing; || though it was a day in which the tribulations rained, I felt nothing.

“I am nothing other than the donkey of my Good”

For two days, it seemed to me that I was always in paradise. After an ecstasy I returned and then as soon as I recovered again I was taken with my dear God. What lessons of humility he gave me! He made me know how much he loves this beautiful virtue and all the good qualities of the world could be possessed but without humility one cannot possess the kingdom and that many souls… here he showed me.

I asked him how they could become proud, what one should have in order to possess this monster that displeased him so much and how one could be aware.

95 He answered me:

Oh, dear love, dear Rosa, your words are very dear to me, you cannot feel it because what is in you || is my work. I said to him:

I fear having trouble with this monster, remove it away from me. You know Jesus, I am afraid.

Do not be afraid, since I am in you, it cannot happen. Oh, what I felt! And I felt very much sinking into my nothingness. I am nothing but the donkey of my Good, because I am very ignorant and I understand very little. I do not know how the others bear me, I am timid, because I do not even know how to speak, and it is true. Sometimes my secretary tells me that they had offended me but, I do not get it because I am truly an ignorant person.

Jesus, my Beloved, puts the beautiful and dear Work upon my shoulders and teaches me to walk. Oh, what a beast I am; my Jesus, how much you must labour! || 96 Oh, Mary my sweetness, you are always my comfort in the atrocious pains in which I am. Oh, help me in the oppression I am experiencing! Oh, how much I suffer! I do not know where such a pain came from, a terrible anxiety that I could not resist. My God, everything which makes me labour seems to me nothing!

With difficulty, I tried to hide my state; to have to combat with this humanity and against it is a terrible thing. What sorrow is this!

Only the tribulations are of comfort to me. The gloom thought, as a dread voice tells me:

You are damned!

And the force that it exerts upon me is such that I agonize. Oh, life, you are hateful to me because you are not capable of doing anything to please my God. Oh, Eternal Father, allow me to scourge myself so that my blood may appease your justice. Yes, I merit it! Oh, cruel pains! ||

97 4. HER EXPERIENCES OF 1878

MS 1.2 – pp. 97-122

“My Love, I cannot bear it anymore!”

1878: How 97 much suffering, my God! – This is what I said

– I am alone!

My poor head and the stomach pained much because I was sick. Today I suffered horrendously more than the other days. Oh, what a torture, my God!

To this, my side was added which gave me sweet but painful spasm! You alone, God, my Beloved know how painful this state of mine was and how I felt worn out. I was almost unable to stand.

Tormented in this way, sorrowful I lay on the cross; as soon as I took a little bit of sleep I was shaken: By whom? By an ugly beast with two very long horns which detached itself from the ceiling to come upon me. When I fixed at it, it stopped at 50 centimeters of distance and folded the legs. 98 I felt a strong pain that I cried and it disappeared; however the pain increased. I took || my Crucifix and I lamented more:

My Love I cannot bear it anymore!

My Beloved did not delay to come to my help and soon I felt united with him. I stayed absorbed in him and my side…

As I recovered, I fainted out of pain; the spasm of the bones was very painful.

“Alone, alone in the midst of the battle!”

Today, because of a strong disappointment connected to many others, I was caught by a melancholy that took me to agony. What did my poor mind experience! Cruel tortures. I was not able to think; I had so much emptiness that I felt fear and compassion. I was unable to pray, as one who finds emptiness on all sides.

That was how I was. My God, accept my pain and give me the strength to || stand in such a torturing state. 99 How painful it was to see clearly that some people, who were supposed to help the Work of God, instead show a false heart and whatever they do is always for something human. Oh, how much the Work of God suffers! Oh, double hearts, how much pain you cause to the most loving heart of Jesus! He does not delay to let me know: they only work out of interest. My God, how much such a sight wounded me! I would never believe that it was possible to suffer so much in spite of my little sensitivity to the earthly things and of my hardness in weeping. This pain drew out my tears and I wept. Oh, what pains I suffer!

Alas, what painful sights! || 100 In this abyss of torturing pains holding tightly to my breast my beloved Crucifix, I asked him: will I live long in such a painful state?

As I said this, my Good seemed to be caressing me and I repeated: Not to run away from pain, because it is very dear to me, you know, my Good that this is my sweetness. My life is suffering. In pain there is your life and your strength. Only this can sustain me; otherwise I would succumb.

I abandoned myself to my God; in him humanity suffers cruel tortures but the soul delights much and becomes beautiful. My Good supplied me with his strength to bear everything. || 101 Alone, without human comfort, I must say that in the torture that I feel there is also contentment and this helps me to desire to be always on the cross; I hold this treasure tightly to my breast and I am happy in such suffering. I even rejoice when I am deprived of the necessary, which means the “temporary” for your Work, my God; how much is still needed of the “spiritual”, my God! And I feel no more life, heaven is closed, for me all the hearts have become like bronze; the earth holds nothing that can comfort me and I do not want anything from it. 102 And I am alone, there is no creature to whom || I can say even a word. No, a cruel sight, you have taken away the minimum support to work!Oh, dear daughters! With sickness I miss the arms for his Work. Alone, alone, worn out in the midst of a battle because of the many suggestions and the cunnings! The dragon always seeks new maneuvers to make me suffer horribly.

The maternal worry for her children returns

After that night, (sometime ago) when the beasts were running on all sides in the room, I was left with fear and it seemed to me that I had a kind of trembling… Oh, what those spirits did! 103 It was horrible! || But my Beloved did not delay to relieve me and kept me so much united to him that

I thought of nothing which does not belong fully to my Good. Oh, how tired I felt and immediately I was absorbed in him! And the side of my heart and my bones how I felt them! In the morning they seemed weak as wax.

104 Today I was very much disturbed by the temptation, that is a diabolic suggestion that repeated to me strongly with a firm voice, that God is displeased because I do not take care of my children; that one day he will ask me a strict account and if something bad befalls them || I will be guilty. Oh, Mary, how can this be! As soon as they were born, they were entrusted to you. Pius IX ordered me to leave them and follow your commands. Oh, my Beloved, I do not know how to describe this torture.

The feeling became always more violent and with shrewdness it told me certain things and within me it made me feel a cruel torture. It said:

  • As you entrusted you children to others, you will be abandoned by all in the last days of your life and beside your bed you will be alone.

Oh, how painful was this disturbance! 105 It seemed that || my head would not stand anymore: sleep was away and also peace, everything was absorbed by such a violent tempest. If I could take a bit of sleep, but the beasts shook me and they appeared to me filthy, horribly ugly, and too shocking that they horrified me. They left me very gloomy and I always thought about the children of whom I must give an account.

Oh, happy day! My Love came to my help, he calmed me regarding my children and he assured me about everything. He took away the spasm and in exchange he gave me peace and resignation for the great misfortunes in his Work. Oh, my sweet Love! || 106 He assured me that my children will be saved and he would never leave them but he would guide them. Oh, what I felt! A peace, a joy that never left me even if I could have the greatest afflictions, they would do nothing to me.

Oh, when I think of those words which remind me that I did the will of my God, I find everything sweet and every pain dear. Oh, my Love, how can I thank you? What can I do? Nothing, because I am nothing, and even less than nothing! Only animated by your strength I am able to do everything. Oh, my Love, how can I keep silent without making you known and loved by all? ||

107 Lessons of Jesus to face much deception and stealing regarding the Work

In these days I received many lessons from my Good and I felt much consolation. Oh, inexpressible joy! And this is what sustains me and gives me strength to face the immense tribulations which are continually in his Work. Who could ever imagine the betrayals, the deceptions, and the astuteness of certain…? Oh, what horror! What could be suspected of someone who pretends to show love towards the Work, and is totally for it, and who even has intimate duties towards the Work but yet betrays, or rather, 108 for a misunderstanding lets down the Work. Oh, if I could say the things clearly what a scene would be manifest. But I do not want because I fear || of offending the charity. What did Jesus do? He allowed me to penetrate and see in the depth of that heart, to the remotest thought. It is true that

I felt a very cruel torture. Many times I felt like fainting but I was always able to remedy it before scandals could occur and the Work could suffer.

How he taught me to carry well this affair! He gave me strength, he caressed me and in the agony which such scenes caused me he sustained me.

Sometimes the fear that it might be the devil that comes to disturb me is mixed. When I see things which require time, because they happen, I say to myself:

  • Certainly it might be the monster who wanted to come to disturb me!

109 Not at all! My Beloved came || to explain to me clearly that he was the one. Many other times my Good left me in agony and he told me nothing; then I suffered terribly and this lasted until the matter took place. When it happened then I feel better, nothing gives me thought; it only leaves me worn out. This last state is painful, and furthermore, I am alone; not even a word can be said to have a suggestion and be alleviated. Oh, terrible pains! Only their appearance makes me anxious; I cannot think and I have only to bear everything with resignation. 110 What a pain this is, my Good! ||

What do I do? I press strongly myself at your feet and hold tightly until the pain had passed; this is my only relief. Oh, how much anguish! Terrible spasms! Oh, what fears I suffer in such a horrendous state!

My soul delights in its Being and stays in peace.

Recovered from pain, nothing is desired, nothing it seems could be sweet on earth, nothing!

Only one thing is felt tasteful: it is charity. Oh, how much joy is felt in being able to benefit and to put right, to reconcile and put in peace with God who is out of the way.

Yes, in charity the soul rejoices, the whole of it shares in seeing the benefit of the creatures; it feels great pleasure. 111 The sacrifice might cost much pain but it always gives || consolation in seeing a soul relieved.

“I live, but I do not live, because

I am always in my Beloved”

Today it seemed that I was freed of melancholy, though I had certain very terrible sights. The unrest has ceased, my mind is clearer and the intellect has started reasoning.

I felt peace within me, a peace… and in suffering much resignation, joy and happiness. It seemed that an interior voice told me:

  • In this tribulation I want you such.

He supplied me with indifference and he still supplies me. I am alone with my beloved Master and I desire nothing. 112 It seems that my Good keeps me as one who is free of any obligation and does not have a share of what || belongs to the earth. I desire nothing, I live fully in my God and I feel to live everything in him. I live, but I do not live because I always stay in my Beloved. However, for the tribulations and horrendous pains, it is not like that; unfortunately, my Love allows that I experience them fully and many times I faint and I agonize cruelly. How many graces my Love, in these days! Where can I find words to thank him? Oh, what I feel sweet Jesus!

This morning, since he wanted that I go to work, he kept me cold, arid and he gave me a certain thrust so that I may come out of the church. Oh, my Love, yes, I go || to work! 113 Here I am to obey your will, transform me in you, suggest to me and teach me; the lights you supplied me with are in fact very great, because there was much need, to guide the souls of the sisters as well as to deal with the affairs of the Work. My Good, even though the disturbances, the pains, the immense affairs of the Work are very many he never allows me to be distracted. Moreover, I feel such an intimate union that if I could not be careful, how many times I could remain absorbed! In fact, many times they ask me:

  • Did you understand? Are you sick?

I give no answer, but unfortunately I am turning aside. Other times, they ask me if I am afflicted. Not at all! 114 It is because I find myself in such an embarrassment… || I go on repeating. My Love, remember your promise, that never anyone would realize.

“A soul from Paradise comforts and foretells me”

I cannot keep quiet about the communication I have with a soul very dear to God, who is in Paradise, and when she was alive she foretold me many things.

In the same way from Paradise she continues. She frequently comes in my tribulations and comforts me and foretells me what will happen.

I asked her about my pains in the hands, on the feet and on the side and soon she consoled me foretelling what will happen to me before my death. 115 I asked her to pray for the Work and for some other things; she answered that it was the will of God. May || his divine will be done in everything and for everything. She said clearly why certain things happened in an affair which I cannot explain well for fear of failing in charity. My Master had already given me an explanation.

I must say that this soul is of great comfort to me. I was very ill and during the sickness, how she comforted me!

While the devil frightened me terribly with horrendous apparitions she comforted me; she assured me that those were all diabolic inventions, that I should not doubt for I would be healed and return as before. What anguish of death this enemy made me feel! One thousand inventions: now dead, now with a covered coffin and || I was always alone.

116 Or at night, how much it did to me! After the midnight, I stayed in peace and even the pain calmed for an hour, then it continued until morning, until I received my Good, this hour I awaited anxiously. Oh, how I counted the hours!

How much goodness for such a disgraceful creature! Oh, infinite bounty, how infinite you are in your mercy!16

The great treasure of charity

27 May, 1878: eve of the Holy Spirit.

After a bad night, my Good came and comforted me; while I was absorbed in him, he taught me what I should do in that state. It continued even in the morning in Holy Communion.

Oh, my Love, what I felt! 117 He told me great things || about his Work and he gave me magnificent lessons.

I remained united the whole day, in the midst of what I had seen and felt; what a day! Immediately I became recollected and remained absorbed. I had to try to distract myself by going around and working; otherwise people would have realized my state. He showed me how and what charity brought in me and how he liked to see me hungry for this treasure, the savor I felt of it and yet never was I satisfied. My Good described to me everything clearly.

My God, how great this treasure in its immensity! 118 You my Good have practiced it || pouring your Blood and dying on the cross for our salvation. Oh, charity!

Special light on purgatory

The other evening, I disciplined myself for the sinners and for myself who is the greatest of them; for the souls in purgatory, and for the holy Church. Oh, what sweetness I felt! I could have fallen into pieces if the obedience of my Love did not stop me. As I completed, my Love, I was enraptured in him. What I saw, what I felt! The things most hidden: he showed me certain imperfections, though I know that I am a heap of infamy. In that union, my Good washed my poor soul which remained purified in the fire of his divine love. Oh, sweetness! As I recovered, I did not do anything other than repeating: 119 I am dying || my Good, if you do not leave me, you will make me die! Let me put into pieces this monster of body, for pity’s sake and remain with you. Oh, how could I live without keeping under beatings this miserable body! Oh, my Love, allow me to scourge it again in order to have the fortune of tasting your delights which are found only in suffering! A thousand words I prayed to him in supplication, but after staying just for a while I was absorbed again and I found myself in my Good.

My Love, who does not love you? All should love you! Is it because they do not know you? What can I do to obtain this? 120 Tell me my dear Love; you teach me very beautiful things, why || don’t you tell me something?

Again, instead of instructing me on this, he gave me beautiful, very profound lessons on his love, and about the souls in purgatory. The latter I asked him because another time I had confused notions; therefore I was left eager to know something about purgatory: what a soul must do in that state, in which it does not suffer anymore but it still remains neglected without being able to see God, and suffers anxiously, but does not suffer the pain it went through when it had to expiate for the sins for which it had been assigned the due pain. 121 In this way it showed me clearly how the souls of purgatory stayed and how the prayers are of relief for them. ||

“How can I live without suffering?”

I cannot describe what pain this poor side is causing me, the bones! Oh, how can I describe it? It is a mixture of consolation and of pains which cannot be described. Oh, Being of my life, only you could tell how I am!

The work is serious, the chains are heavy, and I feel all the iron pieces in my head; but your love makes everything sweet and always more starving of suffering, where I find all my delights. Oh, sweetness! Oh, Love without equal! Tell me, how can I ever live without suffering?

A strong fear assailed me when I was fainting and I thought I would soon breathe my last under the atrocious pain and I was feeling very weak… ||

122 Oh, my Love, perhaps you are not happy that I am carrying so many penances?

But my Good immediately came to my help and assured me that it was his will and he supplied me with the confidence that I had the strength I needed.

THIRD REPORT

MS Booklet 2 (3) pp.1-76

This brief retrospective report might have been written by the Foundress after she obtained the Decree of Praise from the Holy See enacted on 8 April 1876, having overcome well the rough procedure of the Constitutions. The style and also the finality are different from the way she used to express herself in the notebooks properly called Memories. The Foundress felt the need to recount from the very beginning the events of the Work of which she felt herself to be a simple and pure instrument.

However, it is not an impersonal chronicle. Mother Rosa is not able to separate the historic events from her experience of faith and love; she personalized and embodied everything in her suffering and delight, always in relationship with the supreme Good, the Life of her life. This will be later the reason for which having to write the history of the Institute, instead of tracing a realistic history of the events in her book “Travagli e conforti,” she will prefer rather to trust in her ability to narrate it through symbols.

This synthesis of the past is therefore inserted in the series of the Memorie because of the projection of her ideals and the spiritual tensions it contains. For this reason it has an autobiographic value of great interest. It allows us to follow Mother Rosa in the first discovery of herself as Foundress, guided by God, of a Work of which she sees clearly only the fundamental features; though well aware that the acceptance of the divine design will entirely upset her existence, starting from the painful separation from the children and from the parents. We see her a pilgrim in Rome in order to have the verdict of the Vicar of Christ; after she chooses Piacenza as a place destined by Providence far away from her Genoa, and she takes the first steps with the first companions of vocation, with the collaboration of Father Tornatore, facing every kind of difficulty. In all this the personal support of her revered Pius IX was important and decisive.

1. GESTATION OF THE WORK: GENOA FROM 1864 TO 1866

MS 2(3) – pp. 1-51

1 The Congregation of the Daughters of Mary. Order of the Archbishop to review the rules

On February 1864, by obedience, I was a chairwoman of the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary whose director was Frassinetti.1 He had prepared the rules, but not knowing how to go ahead, he went to my confessor to beg him to ask me to accept such duty. 2 My confessor was moved by the cry of Frassinetti and I promised him that I accept because he would have commanded me in virtue || of obedience. That is what happened.

I must say that the mentioned priest came to me; seeing him crying, I was confused and promised to put in order his work, but first I wanted to hear the suggestions of the Archbishop2 on how I have to do it and if he was pleased that I take the duty. Then Frassinetti said that the Archbishop allowed such work but he did not want to approve the rules; he asked me to obtain such approval.

  • 3 It is okay - I answered || a bit confused, fearing that the Archbishop would be against it. We agreed that I would take

the rules to the Archbishop and according to his decision I would have acted.

The next day, I was at the feet of His Excellency and in order and clarity subdued what Frassinetti had told me and what the confessor had ordered me: I had decided to listen to his advice and that it would determine the definitive acceptance. 4 I gave him the rules and || as soon as he saw them, he told me that he knew them and did not want to approve them if those he did not like were not removed from them. I asked him to tell me what he wanted to be removed. He answered:

  • But will Frassinetti be subjected to this?

  • Yes – I answered – because if he does not do so, I will not accept to be what he asks of me.

  • 5 Okay – he answered – I still want one thing in order to give this approval: I want you to guess what displeases me in these rules. ||

  • My God, how will I do?

  • Go and you will return when you have taken the notes. He wanted to listen to nothing and, confused, I went back home.

  • But, how can I guess?

As I reached my room, I put the rules at the feet of my dear

Crucifix. I said: My Love, if I have to obey, you let me know.

And I did not think of it anymore.

When late night came, I took in my arms my dear Crucifix and the rules: tell me, my Love, where are the difficulties which must be removed?

6 In this position || I was enraptured and a voice told me what I should remove, since the Archbishop was right not to approve the rules with those principles because it was not God’s will. Recovered, I embraced and thanked my Good.

Soon I went to the table and skinning that booklet on a paper

I wrote everything exactly as my God had told me.

7 When it was over, I felt utterly beside myself. I folded everything and again I took my dear Crucifix: || I thanked him.

Oh, I clasped him to my breast, my Love! Having said this, I was enraptured again into ecstasy and he himself was dictating to me a Rule; I heard him clearly. This was what he said and what he dictated was very clear; it seemed that this dictation had a different effect.

  • Write down what I have told you immediately.

These were his last words and recovered, I did not delay in obeying. I wrote down exactly what he had dictated to me and kept it carefully. || 8 I returned to pray and nothing disturbed me anymore. The next day, without saying anything, I went to Frassinetti to hear if he was happy that the Archbishop removes what he does not like and to tell him that if he would submit, the Archbishop would approve the rules. With pleasure, he told me that he was ready to accept any amendment and to tell the Archbishop that he could remove whatever he did not like and that he would accept everything.

9 In fact after some days || I went to the Archbishop and told him what Frassinetti had told me. Without telling him anything of how it happened, I gave him the corrections that I had. With surprise, he told me that they were the same as those he wanted to be removed; I copied them again and sent them back and after the approval I handed them over to Frassinetti who was beside himself with joy. But nobody knew of the event.

God wants her Foundress of his Work

10 Those rules I had put aside || began to upset me, because an inner voice constantly tormented me, telling me that I ought to show them, that it was his Work. But I turned away the thought and to say it more clearly, I did not understand what he wanted. One evening:

  • What do you want my dear Crucifix? Why must I show these writings? What is the use?

He answered:

  • For the Work that I desire, it will be great!

My God! I started to think and I did not understand anything: where was this Work to be and who was to found it? 11 I felt so confused || that I stopped thinking and set myself to pray, clinging to my dear Crucifix. A voice that was certainly his, of my Good said to me:

  • I want this Work from you! Show the writing to the

Archbishop.

Oh, how I was confused! Another Work? How can I undertake it? How embarrassing to tell this to the Archbishop!

Oh, my God! I feel my strength will not allow me to do what you command me. I felt as though I were dying. 12 And my children? My Mother? || And I wept. – No Jesus, I do not have the courage, I cannot!

For several days I continued to weep, but I was undecided.

At last I told everything to the confessor, but as soon as he heard this he scolded me and then he ordered me to go immediately to the Archbishop. 13 Weeping I asked him to allow me to write down everything and to send a copy for him. He approved what I asked and soon || he too wanted to read it. Afterwards I wrote a letter in which I narrated what had happened and sent it to the Archbishop. Immediately after reading, he wrote to me asking me to go and meet him. I cannot describe my confusion, the pain; I was shaking as a leaf. I was so upset that as I grasped his feet, it was not possible for me to speak. He realized my state and knowing my disposition, he limited himself to telling me to put into execution the orders of the Lord and that the Work would certainly be very beautiful. || 14 However, there was a need to prepare for those points an internal regulation. I was so confused that I answered yes to everything.

The regulation prepared by the Canon Magnasco

He called me again after few a days and he told me that he would have sent Magnasco, who in that time was a penitential

Canon, so that together with him I could prepare the regulation.3

This in fact came and he tried to put something in order but within me I felt that was not what Jesus wanted.

It happened that Magnasco took the regulation to the || Archbishop but he did not like it at all.

15 He called me and wanted me to tell him if I liked it. I was confused; I did not want to say anything but he ordered me to speak and tell the truth about what I have received and what I did not like in it.

Before I uttered, he said:

  • I do not like it. I want you to sign with your nail so that he might not realize the corrections; basically it is not good. I 16 took it and lightly, I signed with the nail the chapters || which were to be cancelled fully, and with a letter I sent it back to the Archbishop who called me and told me that nothing would be done with that regulation. He himself realized that it was not according to what I received from my God.

The journey to Rome to submit the case of her children

17 I took courage and told him that before writing the regulation, I wanted to meet his Holiness Pope Pius IX, because I hoped that the Holy Father would relieve me from the obedience and certainly he would give the task || to another or nothing would be done.4

I put forward my doubts, saying that it might have come from the devil, since I had two children and a very old father and mother whom I loved very much and it was not possible for me to leave them! And my children…The very thought of leaving them was very painful and I repeated:

  • No, this will never happen, no!

18 The good shepherd allowed me to go to Rome and supplied me with letters of recommendation. ||

It seemed to me that I had already obtained the victory.

  • Never – I repeated – will Pope Pius IX allow that a mother leave her children, a mother for whom I had much

affection and even the poor old father. Both of them loved me much and in the last years it could be said that they adored me.

Oh, no, my Love, you will not allow this. 19 Your vicar will give me peace and relief in such a cruel battle. His word || will be a balm in the wound of my pain which is bitterly open.

I disclosed this desire of mine to my parents and they agreed with pleasure thinking of pleasing me. They supplied me with letters of recommendation and my poor father tried to find a place for me and for my companion on one of the best steamboats to Livorno since there was no railway there yet;

there was only a railway from Livorno to Civitavecchia. My children were both in boarding school. We left the day before the eve 20 of the first of the year || 1866, I mean 28 December of the year that was ending, that is 1865. I reached Rome having suffered horribly because while we were on the steamboat, it was almost two hours after midnight one of the wheels broke and the engine-driver struggled desperately; I fainted and I understood nothing.

The poor captain to whom I was entrusted grieved; the companion was desolate. I remained in that state for hours. 21 I recovered when the steamboat was repaired and moved. I did not want to take anything for relief || because I wanted to reach Livorno without having eaten in order to receive Holy

Communion.

I arrived at noon and immediately I asked to be taken to a church to receive my Treasure. I recommended a poor woman, giving her a good amount of alms so that she might bring a priest to that church.

I heard the Mass because since it was a feast there was Mass at one o’clock in the afternoon. After Mass my companion took me to a bar but I could not take much food; only two small, cold potatoes. || 22 She wanted me to go with her to visit

Livorno, but I was feeling so sick that I could not stand. That is how we went to the station and after sometime we left.

We reached Civitavecchia the next day at five o’clock. I went for the Holy Communion and immediately with a stagecoach we went to Rome; we reached there at one o’clock on 1st January, 1866.

We had Mass in one of the villages where we stopped. 23 I cannot describe what I was feeling. I was given something to restore my strength and then soon people || who were informed about our arrival came.

Audience with Pope Pius IX:

“God will take care of your children, you think of God”

We asked for the audience and it was fixed for the 3rd of January at five o’clock in the afternoon: it was a special audience. Oh, I will never forget this day. My hopes disappeared and a bitter knife pierced me through.

I had already given to the Supreme Pontiff the Rule, I mean what my dear Crucifix dictated me which according to the Holy Father, was like the commandments. 24 I knelt at his holy feet; Pius IX || blessed me, and he raised me with his hand, which was holding mine. He told me that he had already read the Rule and that it was very beautiful. He said that I should not delay to carry it out. Oh, I threw myself to the ground and weeping I said:

  • Your Holiness, I have two children, an old father and mother; my children are both very small.

He answered:

  • It is not of use, God wants this.

  • Oh, no, Your Holiness, God, according to the gospel, will ask me an account of my children!

25 I was || in a fit of weeping.

  • Your Holiness, I love them too much, I cannot leave them, it is impossible!

The Holy Father halted and with a severe voice said:

  • Well, if you do not do what God asks of you, you will have remorse, for the whole time of your life; your conscience will prick and you will have no peace.

I was frightened and:

  • No, Your Holiness, I want to do the will of God.

He answered:

  • Well.

Then in an act as if inspired, he said:

  • 26 This Institute will soon spread like the flight of a dove all over the world. || God will take care of your children; you think of God in his Work.

What a prophecy, dear Holy Father! I stood up and I was hardly able to utter a word. He took me close to his writingdesk and gave me two of his photos writing a saying on each.

Oh, what I felt! Nothing gave me comfort.

  • Father and mother will accept, you will miss nothing, you will be given everything.

I did not understand; he added:

  • 27 I will keep this, you certainly have another copy and you will try to put it in the form of a Regulation.5 ||

I had put, “Daughters of Mary Immaculate” in the heading because I was not only devoted but loving and fully given to Mary. He asked me whether God also gave me the title. I answered no, I had received nothing; it was my desire that they may be called in that way since I am also a Daughter of Mary.

  • I know – said the Holy Father.

From his words, hinted above – whether God gave me also the title – I realized that everything had been written to him.

Assurance on the future of the children: God will take care

28 I was trembling, and he, the Pope was holding me by the hand while tears were flowing down || though I tried to control myself; he comforted me assuring me that my children would be cared for by God in a special way, as eventually happened. On both of them, the hand of God who governed them was visible, and with special graces he kept them under his mantle. Oh, how I physically saw his protection in everything! 29 I did not need to think of them, sure that God was caring for their education and || for their disposal.

This is what happened of my daughter; and he always brought back the son when he ran away; but he never allowed him to belong to the evil societies. What he did was because he had a very good heart, but he came back; he did the spiritual exercises with the friars and they praised him much; he knew how to be loved. I cannot express the love and respect he had for me; it was something extraordinary. He always had in his mouth “mother”; for him it was everything. 30 Certainly || when in the boarding school imprudently they told him that I was a nun he became mad; the blood went to his head and he was not able to reason anymore. But soon, I asked for him to be brought while I was still dressed as a lay woman. As soon as he saw me he cried; then he fixed his eyes on mine and said:

  • Mother, mother!

How can I describe this fact! My heart was breaking but I controlled my emotions so well that he did not realize my unrest. 31 Shaking him I made him observe || that I was not a sister, but dressed as a lay woman; but then he looked at those who were with the habit and he cried. Suddenly he became angry and wanted to beat us not knowing what he was doing. Then I thought of keeping him with me – he was not eleven years old yet – I took him gently and he stayed with me for the retreat and then he received Holy Communion, he did so well that it was a consolation. 98 32 After he went back to the boarding school and gave || signs of a calling to the priesthood and every day he received Holy Communion. The confessor was telling me that I must be watchful over him because he had a tendency for penances and he feared for his health.

In that time I also received the veil and when he saw me he cried very much, but he did not make uproar. I realize that I 33 have gone out of the theme and I am lost; perhaps I should not have narrated certain particular events that only my God knew how much they cost me and how much || I suffered.

How many times I was tempted to abandon everything and to return with them, but I always repeated the words that the Holy Father Pius IX told me. Whenever I met them, I let them know that it was terrible for me that temptation; but the thought of acting against the will of God made me resist any kind of martyrdom and I repeated:

  • I will not have peace for the whole of my life and my conscience will prick me always.

34 What words! And said by the Holy Father with a great deal of || seriousness!

The sacrifice of leaving her children and her parents

I return to the words of the Holy Father when he asked me about the title. Hearing what it was, he said:

  • Well, for now let it be like that, but when you will have the true title, if God wishes it to be another, you will obey and soon the one which the Lord will assign will be written down.

I was silent not knowing what to say; I only said:

  • Yes, Your Holiness, I will obey.

35 The Pope encouraged me with some other words and blessed me and I went home. As soon as I dismissed some of those people who were waiting for us, I locked || myself in my room and started weeping and I continued like that until the next morning. I had lost the sense of touch; my hands, my body and my head were numb. Oh, I was always repeating: my children, my Jesus, my father and mother, I do not have the courage! And I was in an incontrollable fit of weeping; the pain was not so much for my mother and father, (no, about them it was easy for me to resign myself) as it was for my children.

36 I went to kneel at the feet || of the Virgin of Sorrow in the church of Serviti, where I took them after the death of their father, and I handed them to her in such a resolute way that it seemed to me she would take full the care of them and an interior voice assured me of this. Prostrate at the feet of this sovereign queen of sorrows in an incontrollable fit of weeping

I said to her:

  • I must abandon my children; your son’s vicar is ordering me! I am tormented in agony || because I love them much. 37 My mother, you have experienced the desertion of Jesus; to have lost him only for three days, how hard it was for you! Oh, my children! I do not know how to find peace. Leaving them? But where and with whom? Alas, it is too hard! How unhappy I am! I am a mother and I love them very much! Mary, Mary, my mother, what a knife is this: it penetrates till the marrow of my bones! I was absorbed and my tears dried and through the Virgin Mary I began to gain peace and strength. When I came back to my senses, I was transformed, a giant. || 38 I offered generously myself to God and I was repeating the words of Abraham: here I am to fulfill your divine will6 and I will return no more to complaint, nor will I insist on going back.

I offered myself as a victim for his Work. I experienced relief when the Virgin Mary assured me that she would be always with me and that my children will be hers.

Oh, sweet word! That was what happened.

The return journey from Rome. Stopping in Piacenza

39 Meanwhile (I continue from the day following the audience with the Holy Father Pius IX) || I wanted to leave Rome. I wanted to see nothing, I was only saying:

  • Let us go – to my companion.

But she did not want to leave because she liked visiting Rome. In addition, many Bishops and Cardinals were urging me to stay longer so that they could provide for me the things needed for the chapel that I would open and this made things worse. Every time they spoke to me of this, I felt without strength. 40 I received the dispensation from Pius IX7 to keep the Blessed Sacrament. || However, nothing gave me consolation; no, it only brought me pain.

Finally, our return was decided after 28 days of pain. I received many gifts: chalices, ciboriums, the bell, plants, and a very beautiful picture of St. Joseph; at the end they had to prepare packing cases and send them through shipment to Genoa.

41 While on the journey with my companion and a priest whom we met in our lodgings || and who came back with us;

these two suggested me to stop in Piacenza, since I was suffering and also because there were two good souls whom it would be good for me to know. They convinced me and we stopped in a hotel. After some time, two priests came. I told them everything what happened to me and the reason for which I went to Rome. 42 These good priests, as they knew everything, requested me to start the Work in Piacenza, || telling me that it was a peaceful city and the Bishop was good and liked to do good activities. They promised to help me with pleasure and to search for me a suitable lodge.

Therefore, they took the duty of searching for a provisional lodge and afterwards a palace was to be bought, since there were many for sale. 43 How these || plans made me suffer! I was always thinking that time would still be needed. Instead, after some days of my arrival from Rome, I received a letter in which those priests were telling me of having found a suitable house, at a low price. They wanted a quick reply. It took all the strength I had, having already made the gift of myself, to answer that they could fix it, and on the first days of March I would be there with some of my companions, and that was what happened.8

Choice of Piacenza as the cradle of the Work of God

My God, how can I tell this to my father, mother and to the

|| Archbishop? 44 When I reported to the Archbishop on the journey and the audience, I did not speak anything about our stopping in Piacenza for I had no courage.

But he encouraged me and said:

  • Let us get to work.

What did I do? I sent all the necessary things without being noticed by my parents, since my small apartment was divided and it had a free door.

45 With the help of the workers, I forwarded the things || and for this first time I left with the same companion,9 so they thought I was going to visit my daughter who was in Milan in a boarding school. Without saying anything, I went to arrange the rooms, which were rented. I remained there for some days and went back. I already had five of my companions ready to follow me. I told everything I did to the confessor and he was a bit astonished; he feared of my parents and the Archbishop. 46 I took courage and I said everything || to the Archbishop who did not want me to leave Genoa and he told me he would not give me his approval. My God, what can I do?

  • He also told me that he would not accept any resignation from the many associations I was in charge of.

I pleaded with him, but he was adamant. I spent painful days; even the confessor was disapproving the decision I took.

47 What could I do? I threw myself at the feet of the Crucifix: My Love, tell me, was stopping in Piacenza your work || or my illusion? Was I deceived by those people who advised me to do so? If I should not go or if there is anything else I should know tell me. I will accomplish your orders, but free me from this struggle. Let my Archbishop accept and give me his blessing.

A clear voice:

  • What is happening is absolutely in accordance with my will; be calm, everything will be smoothed out.

The heart-rending leave from her parents

48 I needed nothing more, after having thanked my dear Crucifix, full of || trust I prepared myself for the departure. I went back to the Archbishop and I found him reconciled, though he gave me the blessing with pain. He did not accept my resignation; he said that it was enough for me to come back to Genoa every two months and the associations would continue all the same. I kept quiet and then promised to do so.

I resigned from the others, which did not depend on him.

49 In those days, I experienced new things. || At the end I had my parents to persuade. Oh, how hard it was! I went through painful moments; I cannot describe what I felt, for I feel bad.

And yet, I told them without shedding a tear. What a scene to see those two old people! They were watching over me for fear that I would escape at any moment. 50 Finally, the moment came, it was in the morning. The train was leaving at ten and my companions were waiting for me at the station. My mother

|| 51 knowing this sat on the step of the door saying:

  • I want to see if you have the courage, you need to jump over me! My father, whom I had never seen weeping, was in tears and all the others… it 51 was very sad. I took courage and I jumped over my mother10 and I was out. Taking the stairs in a flight I went directly to the station. In this way I started feeling courage like that of a lion. Nothing more could disturb me.

2. THE DIFFICULT LEGISLATIVE JOURNEY OF THE WORK OF GOD

MS 2 (3) – pp. 51-76

The first steps. Encounter with Father Tornatore

As we reached Piacenza, what I passed with those three! Two were bearable but the third! My Jesus, what terrible pains!

Meanwhile, I was searching for a house, always with 52 the help of the Bishop who could provide for me a good lawyer. I found one, which seemed for me suitable and I started negotiations. The day before we arranged the signature of the contract, two of my friends with a priest who came from || Genoa to visit me and to stay two days with me, invited me to go with them to visit a missionary called Tornatore. They said:

  • Let us go to visit him.

I accepted willingly since it was said of him that he was very ascetic. As he saw us, he welcomed us and asked where we were and where we came from. 53 The priest with us told him everything; while we were leaving he said that he || would visit us.

The next day, just the moment I was with the lawyers making the contract, one of my two friends came and told me that the two priests were there. One was Mr.Tornatore. But I was unable to move. Only when something additional was to 54 be done to the contract, was I able to move while the lawyers were writing. I went for a while to greet them, since they were leaving || and I did not see them anymore.

Having done everything in order, we were preparing ourselves for the transfer: but how many troubles; it takes much to speak about everything!

A house, which had nothing but only the exterior! Oh, what could I do! But my God comforted me assuring me that everything was allowed by him.

I had a giant’s strength. Although the work was hard and I was following penitential practices, I felt nothing. 55 At night I did not go to bed; || leaning on the table, I took one hour of sleep and then I resumed work. Sometimes I slept on the floor at the foot of the altar in the chapel or I lay on the cross with a piece of iron or a chain as a pillow where I placed my head, and then so many other penances.

Not knowing where to go for confession, I had the urge to go to Mr. Tornatore, and on the first occasions I was pleased.

Later I felt a sort of fear: || 56 his direction was so different from my previous one. Enough, I soon got over it, because Jesus was my guide in everything and for everything. As we reached the novena of the Immaculate, I asked the Bishop for a priest for the Spiritual Exercises for those who were to receive the habit for the day of the Immaculate. He gave me Mr.Tornatore.11

The sisters were two from the first group and three who entered after when we were already in our own house. 57 He gave the retreat and on the day of the Immaculate || these five sisters were clothed with the religious habit.

Origin of the name of St. Anne given to the Institute

I now retrocede to say how the name of St. Anne came and how the saint herself showed me to how the veil should be. As soon as we came to this house, I chose a small room that could be good for the chapel, which the Bishop blessed and left for the Lord. Oh, how happy I felt to have my Beloved with me!

And I spent entire nights there; oh, what nights || I had!

58 One of those evenings, when I was alone in prayer and I was very much in an intimate union with my God, the chapel became resplendent with light and the Blessed Virgin appeared to me with St. Anne; a little lower, as though he were kneeling towards the Blessed Virgin was St. Francis of Assisi. The Immaculate with a clear voice said:

  • I want that the title of the rules be: “Daughters of St. Anne” my mother – and here, she pointed to her - I leave this work to my mother with great satisfaction. || 59 Do not grieve; for I will consider to be done for me everything you do for her.12

After the last words, the three of them disappeared. I was enraptured and it seemed to me that I could see them still, but I said nothing. I remained like that for a long time and then I came to my senses. I saw that a long time had passed. What can I do? 60 I was thinking of the obligation of informing the Holy Father, since the title was given to me, because the commandments were already printed with the title of the Immaculate. || I had no peace and I did not want anybody to know about it. This was a torment.

Meanwhile, I wanted to inform the Holy Father so through Cardinal Patrizi I sent a letter.13 Soon, he ordered that they should be called by that name and that I should soon write the regulation. 61 This happened before the vestition and after it had some modifications. || The thought that Pius IX wanted the internal regulation tormented me. I prayed a great deal but I never heard anything at all.

One evening, while I was alone in the chapel, St. Anne and Father Bernardo appeared to me. I recognized him because Mr. Tornatore had given me the picture. In this way I was confused; 62 the Holy Mother was beautiful in the act of caressing me. She made herself very close to me and communicated to me such a powerful love for her, I must confess that I was at a loss as to adapt to it and love her as || a mother.14 Father Bernardo said these words to me:

  • Tell Father Tornatore to write the regulation that you want.

They both vanished. The love for St. Anne had so powerfully penetrated me that it took away whatever unwillingness was left in me, and it became very strong. In this way I invoked her in all my needs and I always found satisfaction: in providence, in my journeys, in everything. 63 She remained so deep in me that I had her always || before my eyes. “Oh, my Mother,” I always exclaimed.

Apparition of Father Bernardo. Father Tornatore author of the Rule

I did not have the courage to tell what Father Bernardo said to Mr. Tornatore. I waited for several months and the second time Father Bernardo came alone and exhorted me to go soon to Mr. Tornatore. I told him that I was not able to overcome myself because I was ashamed and said:

  • I cannot go, why don’t you go to tell him?

I answered in this way to Father Bernardo, who said nothing, but only:

  • You must obey!

  • I cannot! ||

64 Finally, one morning after Holy Communion, he came close to me:

  • I tell you that you must obey!

I did not answer him because I had my God with me and I had a lot to tell him. After a while, perhaps a week - at least it seemed to me – there he was again. I was concluding my thanksgiving, when I suddenly heard a scolding voice. 65 I looked, it was Father Bernardo. In a resolute tone he said threateningly:

  • Go straight away and tell him that it is I who send you; || that he should soon prepare the regulation.

How much pain I felt! But I decided to go and I went. I went to Mr. Tornatore and I told him half of what Father

Bernardo had told me. He started laughing and answered:

  • I will write them.

The succession of the writing of the first Rule

And he did. 66 As soon as it was printed I took it to Rome and all the members of the Sacred Congregation of Bishops and Regulars made a fool of me because the Rule was written in a form of a dialogue: the mother St. Anne spoke and the daughter replied. ||

One asked if I always spoke with St. Anne. What a shame I suffered together with my secretary Sister Anne Vincenza! I did not have the courage to return there.

I also gave a copy to the Holy Father, and he encouraged me. He said that he would read it. The words of this Holy Father Pius IX were consoling to me.

I returned to Piacenza. I leave out what I went through. 67 After some months, a respectable person || wrote to me asking me to withdraw the Rule from all the Bishops who had a copy, and all the copies I had in the house and to burn them. I soon followed the notice. Since Mr. Tornatore had been condemned, he should not meet the Daughters of St. Anne, nor should he come into the house. No one should go to him for confession. 68 In the evening when he came I communicated all this to him. || He also told me to leave for Rome and I left soon. Oh, how much pain!

Welcomed by Pius IX.

The encouraging words of the Pope

As soon as I arrived in Rome, I went to Monsignor Vitelleschi, the secretary of the Sacred Congregation of Bishops and Regulars. He said:

  • You received a hard blow!

He was prepared to meet the Holy Father and he told me that he would tell the Holy Father that I was in Rome; he wanted to be alone to tell me:

  • Do you know that if Mr. Tornatore was in Rome he would have been taken to the Holy Office? What did he do! You keep firm the spirit || of the Work, that is what is needed; afterwards you will receive other instructions.

69 He left me and I went home very upset that I did not know what to think. In the evening, the same Monsignor Vitelleschi sent me two lines in which he informed me that the Holy

Father, being aware of my arrival was waiting for me the next day at ten in the morning. As soon as the great saint saw me:

  • 70 Courage, do not pain, the Work should go ahead, you must only remove from that Rule all that || the Protector will tell you. I want the regulation to be written by you only; the

Lord will help you, keep firm the spirit.

He continued telling me to leave aside that priest, that is Tornatore, because it was better, since I would finally enjoy peace and had no need to suffer much. Then he paused to comfort me; I called my secretary, the Pope blessed her encouraging her. || 71 I thought:

  • Who would have told him about the pains, for he said that

I was suffering because of Mr. Tornatore?

It was true, but I have never said to anyone what sufferings

I went through. For how much I inquired I drew nothing, only after a long time I came to know; at least I hope not to be mistaken.

The writing of the text of the Constitutions.

The decree of approval

Being in peace with the words of Pius IX, which gave me life, I went to meet the Protector who was also leaving. 72 I did not go immediately because the secretary came to meet me and we arranged || that I should leave after the audience with the

Holy Father. This was what I did. In the afternoon I went (…)

to his Excellency Vanicelli, who welcomed me joyfully. After sending out the secretary he communicated to me the letter of the Sacred Congregation of Bishops and Regulars. 73 I already knew the first part; the second part said that I should go to Ferrara close to the Protector. Regarding the Rule I was to be careful to have no more communication with that priest and formulate them under the direction of || his Excellency

Vanicelli. I promised to obey to the letter. I only asked to go back to Piacenza to pick up the daughter I left there – we had already a house in Ferrara. He was also leaving for Ferrara. I arrived some days later, and immediately started writing and as I finished the first part I took it to him.

He was pleased, but being unable to engage himself he told me that he would submit everything to Monsignor Giordani. 74 In this way every chapter that I wrote was revised by Monsignor Giordani. || One day he asked me:

  • If I would agree to listen also the superior of the Augustinians if the Rule was in order.

He sent the Rule, but the Augustinian superior wanted to make some additions which were not good; the same Cardinal informed him that they were not needed. With the help of God I finished them and the Cardinal took them to Rome. 75 I also went back and soon when I met the Holy Father he told me that he recommended the Sacred Congregation to hasten || the revision for the approval. I received the decree of approval.15 dition, look at Letters, II, pp. 12-18; Iv, pp. 288-291).

Light she received on the shape of the habit

My life was a continuous going around, now for foundations of houses and then for collections in order to maintain the sisters. I offered everything, even my pains to

God and united with him, his poor slave lived, if it could be said to have life, because only my Master, my All - I can assure

  • was leading me as a child. I will also say how I received the clothing: the time of clothing was nearing || and I still knew nothing. 76 One morning I was alone in the chapel because it was very early. I prayed to the Holy Mother and I saw clearly, with my open eyes, the saint who showed me the shape of the veil:

it was spread; she was holding it with two hands. It stayed for five minutes and then it disappeared. Another time she showed me the cap, and she was dressed with our habit. Oh, how much impression it left me! The veil was internally detached; I heard a voice that explained as if it were being put on another person.

It seems to me that I had not minimally changed anything.

FOURTH REPORT

MS Booklet 5.1 – pp. 1-14 (additional parcel)

Added to booklet 5.1 of the Memorie is found a parcel of 14 pages with a vivid and evocative narration in which Mother Rosa remembers how she discovered to be destined by God to give life to a religious institute. It was her sense of Church that made her accept the will of God in obedience to her hierarchical superior, the Archbishop of Genoa Monsignor Andrea Charvaz and after in the supreme decision of Pope Pius IX, whose answer she held as inspired by God: “God will take care of your children.”

In the manuscript, there is no indication of the date of this brief writing. It has no addressee or better, as in all the Memorie, the addressee is herself. From the repetition of the theme of the children in her pages it could be deduced that the thought of not attending and caring for the education of her children very often weighed heavy on her conscience. It was one of the temptations with which the devil tried to disturb her. That is why she needed to find the justification of that sacrifice in the words of Pius IX.

Since the contents are the same as those of the third report, which is more ample, no notes of clarification are needed.

The Rule of the Daughters of Mary

Obedience! While I was a superior general in the

1 Congregation of the Daughters of Mary, a very good priest had prepared the Rule and he wanted the approval of Archbishop Charvaz of Genoa. But the Archbishop refused. Aware that the Archbishop directed me and I could obtain much from him, the above mentioned priest asked me to insist in order to obtain the approval.

I did, and the Archbishop told me that it was enough to remove what he did not like and he would approve them.

  • 2 Well - he added – take it with you and after I want to see if you are able to find out. ||

During the night, while I was kneeling at the feet of my dear Crucifix, I saw clearly what the Archbishop did not like.

Soon I woke up and signed it; again kneeling I was thanking him and I heard a voice coming out from the same

Crucifix; he dictated to me certain Rule. I was bewildered:

  • What will ever be?

  • Write down.

In this way he concluded. I woke up and wrote. I went back to pray and I felt something in me which I could not understand.

When it was day I went to receive Holy Communion.

3 Oh, what a union. || I received consolations; I saw great things and an interior voice said to me:

  • Speak to the Archbishop about it.

I responded:

  • No, no!

I went to the Archbishop and I took to him the Rule of the Daughters of Mary. He was happy because I had guessed perfectly. He said:

  • If the priest is ready to remove these, I will approve it.

That was what happened.

But I said nothing. The next day, again an interior voice whispered to me:

  • Obey!

  • Oh, no, my God, I feel ashamed!

  • Take them to the confessor.

  • I cannot, I feel ashamed.

What pains! 4 And I never understood what he wanted to do with that Rule. || I continued to ask him but in an impelling and severe manner he made me understand that he wanted it. I was upset and I spoke to the confessor who had much difficulty understanding. Because of the shame that I felt, I did not want to speak outside the confessionalbox, but only when I went to confession. The voice of the Lord reproached me a great deal. 5 In the same way the confessor was reproaching me and telling me that if I resisted in obeying the Lord || he would punish me. What days! What pains! What agony!

My thought was always fixed on a terrible battle. I was studying a way of carrying the Rule to the Archbishop without having to speak with him, but after I said to myself:

  • After reading it he will send for me and he will know how it happened. My God! I will die of shame; I cannot bear only thinking about it.

“I cannot! I have children”

What pains! What martyrdom! At the end in this violent state I was not able to resist. 6 I decided || to write and it happened as I expected. As soon as he read the Rule he called me and as soon as he saw me he said that it was the will of God to carry out what has been suggested to me.

I answered:

  • Oh, have pity, I have two children and an old father and mother who love me very much, and I love them in the same way.

The thought of leaving my children – no, I cannot – it was stronger than me. And he added:

From the Rule you received, the will of God is clear for the foundation of an institute. || 7 Therefore carry it out…

  • I cannot! God will raise up another one but not me! I have children and the Lord will ask me a strict account. We battled and then he left me saying :

  • Think about it and do the will of God.

He gave me the writing but he kept my Rule; he gave me the copied one. Patience!

What days of struggle! He sent me Magnasco, who in that time was the penitential Canon. He formulated another

Rule. 8 Nothing moved me though he was telling me:

  • Decide.

The || confessor said the same; but seeing my children and the parents I was feeling torture. I tried to find peace, I asked for light from the saints, but in one voice they answered me:

It is the will of God.

The journey to Rome and the answer of Pius IX

What should I do? I decided to go to the Holy Father

Pius IX, and that is what I did. As I arrived in Rome, I handed him a copy of the Rule and the next day, I was received in a special audience.

9 As soon as I was at the feet of the Holy Father – I leave out narrating what I suffered while waiting, it was so painful, || unbelievable and could not be imagined: a continuous pain that I was about to faint. Oh, terrible pains! The first words that he said were:

  • You must do the will of God; it is the Work of God;

you should not forbear doing what God wants.

Oh, what a command! I started arguing:

  • Holy Father, I have two children and the holy gospel says that before all else we should guard and bring up well our children because we will be asked an account. He answered:

  • No, God will take care of your children.

  • I have old parents; I have no courage to leave them.

He answered:

  • 10 God will take care. ||

And me:

  • Oh, Holy Father, I cannot do such obedience: my children…

And he in a gentle manner:

  • Do not doubt, God will take care of them and you think of his Work which as fast as the flight of a dove will spread all over the world. Courage!

He raised me up and gave me two small gifts writing a saying on his photograph. My chest was tightening and I was not able to speak to him anymore.

He added:

  • Woe betide you, if you do not do the will of God, your conscience will prick you throughout || your life.

11 How could I answer?

  • Yes, I promise to obey Your Holiness.

But the tears were choking my throat; I was unable to say a word.

I always had a companion with me when I went out. Hearing what was said, she rejoiced. In contrast, I was stifled. All those who were in the house and those who came congratulated me cheerfully. As for me, I was sad. 12 As soon as they left and it was nine o’clock in the evening, I locked myself in my room. I had the audience at || five in the afternoon – and I wept until the next morning. My companion found me leaning; I had lost the sense of touch and I seemed woody, exhausted. After some time, I went to receive Holy Communion. I always repeated: What pains!

  • How can I leave my children? Oh, how awful is God’s judgment! Jesus, have mercy on me and on my children!

I cannot think of it, I feel the agony, it is too much! 13 Mary, dear mother, you know how important one’s children are, || since you are a mother. And one’s elderly parents?

As I reached home I found all the privileges written by the hand of Pius IX for the chapels and very many gifts for the churches which were to be opened. All brought something, one better than the other, but nothing dissuaded me; instead they increased my pain. 14 Two very big packed cases were sent through shipment. They were all full of sacred furnishings, chalices, ciboriums and many other things. Oh, what pain this caused me! || I wanted to leave soon and I suffered much in the travel both to and fro.

At the end, when I arrived in my family home only my God could describe my pains!

THE YEARS OF GENOA THE BEGINNING OF THE INSTITUTE IN PIACENZA

RETROSPECTIVE REPORT MEMOIRES * By mistake Mother Rosa anticipates by a year the “liberation from all bonds”. Her husband Jerolamo Custo died on March 9, 1858.

1 Rosa Gattorno, in the years of her “conversion”, experienced the influence of the Sons of St. Francis and discovered in the saint of Assisi a certain spiritual affinity, a model, in her longing to share in the suffering of the Redeemer. She started to girdle the rope of Saint Francis and later she wore the habit of the Franciscans and made the profession as a member of the Tertiary Order. In the Memoirs she frequently mentions the saint, calling him: “My Father.”

2 At that time Rosa Gattorno had as her spiritual director Father Joseph Firpo, keeper of the metropolitan church. He was of great help to her in the first years of widowhood, in the moment of her decision to consecrate herself to the Lord, and during her stay in San Francesco d’Albaro.

3 The first autobiographer of St. Francis of Assisi, Tommaso da Celano wrote that St. Francis desired, “to offer to God all the fibers of his heart in multiple holocaust” (Vita II, 95); but the expression taken by Mother Rosa is rather attributed to St Francis of Sales.

4 “It is not me who lives but Christ lives in me” (Gal 2: 20). Mother Rosa very frequently repeats these words of St. Paul, which express the experience of life in Christ.

5 The Order of Penance or Third Franciscan Order, today called Franciscan Secular Order, required a period of preparation for novitiate and then the profession of a Rule, which at the time of the entry of Mother Rosa, was still that promulgated by Pope Nicolo IV in 1289.

6 Here, as ahead, Mother Rosa interrupts the autobiographical narration in order to describe the state of interior suffering that she feels while writing.

7 The moment of the sacrifice of her will, which in the mystical ascent signs the decisive step towards the infused experiences, will be remembered by Mother Rosa with exact precision in her book Travagli e Conforti, where it becomes the leading thread of the fascinating adventure (Cf. la nuova edizione, Roma 1992, pp.38, 50, 176, 308f, 324,467).

8 It was a small crucifix which Mother Rosa carried tightly tied on her chest for more than five years. It is kept among her relics in Piacenza.

9 Mother Rosa applied this blessed oil to the sick trustful in the good effects that she saw. Regarding this, Cardinal Granito di Belmonte testified in the beatification process: “I remember when she was asked for prayers of

healing, she prayed and she gave out the oil which she called of the Eternal Father, towards whom she had special devotion. Many times the sick were healed” (Summarium, p.38).

10 Cf. Mt 5: 30: “And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away.”

11 Beginning from 1862, Rosa Gattorno experienced every now and then the pains in the feet, the hands and the side, an effect of the contemplation of the Passion. This time, however, it seems that she received the gift of the invisible stigmata but with clear exterior reflections. On some occasions the wounds became visible (cf. L.RIARTE, A Spiritual Portrait of Mother Rosa Gattorno, pp. 106-111; Summarium, p.85). The fact that this important mystical experience is found after the others of the year 1866 until now made me date it on 1st January 1867, during a hypothetical journey of Mother Rosa to Rome in that period. But there are no indications of such a journey. From the comparison of the first and third reports, which under different retrospective evocations, put the arrival at Rome on 1st January, the succession of facts could again be completed. Mother Rosa and her companion, Teresa Porta, made their last stage of journey from Civitavecchia to Rome during the night between 31December 1865 and 1st January; she wrote: “The whole night I was always with Jesus and Mary.” In the morning, taking advantage of the stage-coach, they were able to attend the Mass in a church of a town. Mother Rosa, who in her letters does not follow the reckoning of 24 hours which was used in Central Italy, but the distribution in two spaces of 12 hours, specifies that the arrival in Rome was “at one of the 1st January 1866.” Therefore, it was one pm. After a brief “relief”, she welcomed the people who were informed in advance of their arrival. She asked for a private audience with the Pope, which was granted on 3rd January. In spite of the tiredness of the journey, the Servant of God, who during the night and the following morning was almost out of herself, still wanted to go to the Lateran to climb the Holy Stairs. That was the time she was raptured in God with the effects that she describes being prolonged during the night and the following day. All this shows with how much intensity she lived the preparation for her encounter with Pius IX.

12 The French-Prussian War was on one side; on the other side was the uncontainable advance of Garibaldine army towards Rome. These kept the people in an atmosphere of apocalyptic presage. The fatal year will be 1870. Paris will suffer the consequences of a long siege. Rome instead will surrender to the soldiers of the light infantry almost without battle. Look at the interpretation of the biographer A.M. Fiochi, La Serva di Dio Rosa Gattorno, ed. riveduta e ampliata, Roma 1996.

13 The service to the poor sick, in their homes and in the hospitals, was the primary apostolate of the Daughters of St. Anne in the first period. In this work of charity, the Foundress found much consolation, seeing in every sick person the suffering Christ.

14 These pages were written in the weeks preceding the siege and the fall of Rome, 20 September 1870. According to the historic reading, frequent in people of faith, Mother Rosa sees God’s punishment in the victory of the liberal forces.

15 In the pages of the Memoirs, very often we find parenthesis with exclamations of pains and swelling on the “side of the heart” or even “my side” generally in moments of great fervor or unitive experiences. It is the fire of love. That is how it is understood. It causes a true painful swelling, sometimes producing pressure on the ribs: a mystical phenomenon that we read about in the lives of many saints.

16 Rosa Gattorno slept lying on a wooden cross spread over a straw mattress.

17 The Foundress frequently remembered the answer she received from Pius IX on the duty of caring for her children. Look at the detailed narration in the third and fourth autobiographic reports.

18 Mother Rosa received from Father Giovanni Battista Tornatore the devotion to the Venerable Bernardo Maria Clausi of the Order of the Minims, who died considered holy in Paola in 1849. She felt helped and comforted by him in a very special way.

19 The expression, often repeated, “This heart of his,” denotes the mystical experience of the change of hearts that she had in Genoa at the beginning of her total consecration to God.

20 She left the phrase incomplete for spiritual modesty before certain hidden favors; it is the scar that remained after the wound of the side healed, an experience she had many years earlier. As we will see, the scar was opening and bleeding every now and then.

21 Look above, note 19.

22 In the small room of Piacenza, among the other instruments of penance, a big wooden cross was venerated that was leaning vertically against the wall. On it Mother Rosa tied herself, as though nailed up, for a better participation with Christ crucified (cf. Summarium, pp.260, 711).

23 Look above, note 19.

24 For some years Mother Rosa speaks of this “bright cloud” which comes to her help, clearing her uncertainties, revealing to her the hidden things, making her to regain peace and courage in difficulties. In truth it is the same supreme Good that supplies the absence of guidance of a director.

25 On the date in which Mother Rosa wrote, such a foundation did not exist. Perhaps she saw the realization of the prophecy in 1884, when the community of the Tertiaries of St. Anne, Perpetual Adorers of the Blessed Sacrament, formed by the dumb-deaf had its beginning.

However Carlotta was feeling called to the life of matrimony; when she was 23 years old, she got married to Count Gaspare Barbiellini Amidei.
